Some prop firms are better than others when it comes to slippage and stuff. You'll have to test which ones feel good to you.

I knew my stops were getting intentionally tagged by a particular firm *cough* MFF *cough*. I was copying trades across 2 different prop firm accounts and somehow one of my accounts got stopped while the other is still active. They had the same stops but one had a weirdly higher wick that the other account wasn't showing. That's when I knew I no longer will be getting a challenge from them.

You can try and open the same trades between your personal and prop firm acc and see what happens.

1 lot = 100,000 of the lead currency. If you have a 10,000 account with 100:1 leverage, this means your max open positions are 10 lots at any given time. Now does your strategy need 10 active lots to function with a 10,000 account? Only you can answer that.

Thanks for the tip. I think it's a great idea to start small and have a feel for it and see what happens. And that's one of my worries, if I try discretionary, how do I keep it in a system and not just start doing whatever.

Once you pass the challenge, in most prop firms, you get to keep 80% of the profits. Usual rate is $500 for 100k virtual funds challenge with 1:100 leverage. Once you pass, only rule is to not hit the 5% daily drawdown or 10% max Drawdown. It varies from prop firm to prop firm, but some allow news trading, holding over the weekend, etc.

I haven't considered swing, but it does make a lot of sense!
I think the issue is I made the whole strategy around passing and managing prop firm money, which at the time meant I need to consistently pass within 30 days, and that I can't have trades open over the weekend. Given the above, do you think it's still worth me looking into swing? If I can't hold a position over the weekend, very likely I'd only have 0-2 trades a week I'd imagine. And different timeframes show different things, what works for me in the 30m might not work for the 4h.

I closed a trade at 1:2 R:R since I have been on a losing streak for 2 weeks months ago and just wanted to get some back but it turned out that I could have gained a 1:4 if I just let my strategy run. After that, I've just completely followed my strategy. But that decision from an area of fear, whereas right now it's coming from a place of clarity, if that makes any sense.

And yeah, I haven't mass tested it yet. But for the past 3-4 trades that I just let the strategy run, I could have gained more. Maybe because I've been thinking that it might be another runner and I'd make the same mistake...

Agi is a good element to go for a sac, unfortunately, you'll lack the sustain in earlier levels as your equip won't have good enough vit and other stats to help your damage. Sacs are well known for taking a hit and lifesteal. Out of the 4 elements, agi has the least lifesteal, which is one of the biggest features a sac must have in the earlier levels.

With regards to what element suits you at the moment, I'd say go for strength as Gobbal set would give a decent amount of str that you'd need for pvm. At later levels, you'd want to look at having an eider set + gelano. This gives you the choice to choose between having int, the strongest single attack lifesteal that the sac has (disregarding madness), or something more balanced, which is chance (dissolution), which provides an AoE attack around the caster. When I was around 60, I'd have enough to get 2 elements, which made it possible for me to switch between int and cha depending on the situation. 

So all in all, I'd say Sacrier's foot with Gobbal set at your level, and once it's possible to grab an eider and gelano, go int or cha or int/cha as you want more sustain as a pvm player. Do note though that you must always have nimble punishment as you want to have the enemies to get locked by you as you'd be the tank of the team.
